correctness.rationale: The frozen proof and verification omit a required inclusion: Euler identifies the chart ideal with (f,f_t,f_s), not (f_t,f_s). The frozen theorem is not false; the replacement result and verification prove f=(t+t^q)f_t+(s+s^q)f_s directly, closing the gap. The ideal is then (A²,B²). The homogeneous partials exclude x=0. Elimination gives H(s)=s^(r+1)+κs^r+1 with r=q(q+2)/4 even, H'=s^r and H(0)=1, hence r+1 simple roots. At each root the Jacobian of (A,B) has nonzero determinant s^(q/2), yielding the claimed completed local algebra. As a separate length check the full quotient is free of rank two over K[s,s^{-1}]/(H²). This applies also at q=2 and k=0.
residual_risks: Symbolic Jacobian calculation, not formal proof-assistant verification; no conclusion about branch or conductor invariants.
